newsitem.title: USA: FedEx to up capital spending in fiscal '98.
newsitem.headline: FedEx to up capital spending in fiscal '98.

text.p: Federal Express Corp will boost capital spending in fiscal 1998 by 15 to 20 percent over fiscal 1997, company officials said Monday.

"We have a terrific international business going, earnings are growing...now's the time to put the pedal to the metal," Alan B. Graf Jr., chief financial officer, said in a conference call with reporters.
Graf said the company will spend about $2.3 to $2.4 billion in fiscal '98, up from under $2 billion in fiscal '97.
Part of the fiscal '98 amount will go toward purchasing 22 wide-body jets, plus investments in computers and delivery vehicles including trucks, Graf said.

Earlier Monday, Federal Express reported fiscal fourth- quarter earnings of $1.14 per share, beating Wall Street's estimate by $0.05 per share. The company posted earnings of $1.01 per share in the year-earlier period.

Graf said fourth-quarter results were bolstered by strong performance in Federal Express' international segment. International operating income rose to $59.4 million from $37.2 million in last year's fiscal fourth quarter.
